topic.title: Your 'free' WhatsApp support just started billing you
topic.claim: The WhatsApp chat you use for refunds isn't free anymore, and the cost just got passed to you.
topic.behaviour: Brands now pay per customer-service reply on WhatsApp, so many are slowing responses or pushing you to a chatbot instead.
topic.mechanism: Meta found a way to charge for the one support channel everyone got addicted to. The cheapest fix for a business is to make the human part scarcer.
topic.group: Anyone who messages brands on WhatsApp for order or refund updates
topic.moment: You message a brand's WhatsApp for a refund update, and a bot keeps looping you instead of connecting you to a person.

turn.believed: WhatsApp support is free, that's why every brand uses it.
turn.actually: Brands now pay per reply, so the easiest cost-cut is making it harder to reach a human.

topic.because: Every reply past 1,000 a month now costs the business money, so the incentive flips from 'answer fast' to 'answer less.'

proof.fact: ₹0.115 per message (about ₹0.136 after GST) after the first 1,000 free messages a month

topic.payoff: The chatbot that won't let you speak to a human isn't bad design. It's a bill being passed down to you.
topic.send_to: Anyone who's noticed customer support getting slower lately.
real_details: 8,000 monthly replies now cost roughly ₹1,085 before tax
topic.news_peg: Meta's WhatsApp Business API pricing change effective Oct 1, 2026
topic.why_now: Change just landed; the slowdown is about to become visible to users

score.why: Everyone's fought a brand's WhatsApp bot; the because, Meta charging per reply, flips 'bad support' into a bill quietly passed to you.
